title: Digital F(r)ictions
description: Digital F(r)ictions is a research-creation project selected for MAMBO’s Digital Residency, organized by the Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá. Developed together the Digital Visual Studies team, the project uses artificial intelligence to explore and reinterpret Bogotá through the lens of the museum’s digital collection. By analyzing visual and textual features from artworks, the project constructs new artistic and urban narratives, offering critical reflections on both the city and the role of AI in cultural institutions. The initiative merges curatorial practice with machine learning, re-signifying the MAMBO Collection while addressing ethical and cultural dimensions of digital technologies.

title: Fly-Meet
description: Fly&Meet is a non-profit project that provides a platform to find affordable shared destinations among multiple origins. People from different places find the most comfortable destination for both parties. Technically, it leverages the Kiwi API to make multi-origins flights search and filters the results to show the cumulatively cheapest destinations.  Interestingly, the platform reveals the hidden geography of the aerial network where the most affordable destinations between two nodes might fall far from their middle location.

title: 3D Visibility study
description: Result of a collaboration with the italian mobility firm Systematica, the web-app functions as a data-visualization platform for the stakeholders involved in the Scalo Porta Romana project in Milan. It showcases several layers of a three dimensional visibility study. Rather than a simple report, the platform permits an active interaction with the data, which remains queriable to filters and selections. In this manner, actors involved in the development process used the platform to discuss the positioning of emergency signs, benches, and other visibility-dependant amenities.

title: Multipli(city)
description: Halfway between a mental map and an index, the multipli-city navigator collects the outputs of a PhD seminar led by D. Negueruela del Castillo, G. Savicic and I.Neri at EPFL, Lausanne. Leveraging the powerful open-source Leaflet and the minimal Alpine JS packages, it permits a twofold reading of its content in the form of pamphlets and conceptual diagrams spatially placed in a fictitious geography

title: Cities Matchmaking
description: Cities Matchmaking is a platform to inspect the results of the homonym publication developed together with Erze Dinarama for the opening chapter of The Routledge Handbook on Greening High-Density Cities edited by Peng Du, Kheir Al-Kodmany, Mir M. Ali. The visualization shows in an interactive fashion the study carried out on a set of global cities  (approx 4500) in the search of ecological twins to support international collaboration projects in the face of climate changes. More precisely, the research produces 7 map indicators for every city, later analyzed for similarity via Machine Learning algorithms.

title: Emerging Assemblages
description: Emerging Assemblages: Navigating Shifting Ecologies is a digital platform that hosts the research behing the Kosovo Pavilion at the Venice Biennale 2025. The website serves as a dynamic space to explore the themes and narratives presented in the pavilion. More specifically, the pavilion explores shifting seasonal patterns and ecological disruptions, particularly in relation to agricultural change and species migration.

title: Itzal
description: Awarded best idea at the Basque government’s open data contest (2022), Itzal - or Shadow” in Euskara - is a routing web app to fight the harsh spanish summer sun. It allows users to see pathways that minimize exposure to sun at different times of the day. Thanks to this alternative route, users can reduce risk to sun heat and high temperatures in order to avoid possible dizziness, sunstroke and heat stroke and improve the experience of active and healthy mobility throughout summer. Technically it exploits a mix of 3D modeling and climatic forecasting to evaluate ad-hoc shortest paths over a road graph.

title: Mimesis and Machinic Agency
description: 'Mimesis and Machinic Agency' is an experimental study on multimodal machine learning models, exploring how art emerges from recursive translation loops between image and text. Presented at the xCoAx 2024 conference, the work introduces a generative autonomous loop iteratively transforms prompts and visuals, gradually diverging from the original input. Its evolution is analyzed through computational metrics and critical interpretation, highlighting uncanny outputs that provoke new debates on machinic agency and aesthetics.

title: Clip and the City
description: Clip and the City' investigates how artificial intelligence can reveal the interplay between history, architecture, and urban development. Using 360° panoramic images analyzed by vision-language models (CLIP & OpenCLIP), the project examines how mainstream culture is embedded and interpreted by machine learning systems. Through spatial analysis of the generated embeddings, we identify cultural clusters and discontinuities within Rome’s urban fabric, uncovering hidden narratives and biases. This computational approach, resembling a forensic exercise, highlights how contemporary imagery and AI models can shed new light on the historical and social dynamics of cities

title: Cityscapes Transformed
description: Cityscapes Transformed: Immersive Exploration at the Intersection of Culture, Computation, and Curatorial Practices” explores how machine learning can reframe urban and cultural narratives. Developed for the 2023 Helsinki Art Biennial in collaboration with the Centre for Digital Visual Studies (MPG, University of Zurich) and artist Yehwan Song, the project reinterprets the Helsinki Art Museum’s collection by embedding unexhibited artworks into computer-generated 360° panoramas of the city. Through a web-based interactive platform, visitors can navigate this speculative geography where cityscapes and artworks merge, inviting new reflections on curatorial practices, machinic aesthetics, and audience engagement.

title: VORD
description: VORD (Visual Open Research Data) is a swissuniversities-funded project that develops innovative techniques for extracting quantitative insights from large-scale cultural heritage datasets. By combining advanced machine learning models for color, composition, and semantic embedding analysis, VORD shifts from whole-image interpretation to fine-grained, object-level understanding. This methodology enhances model transparency and interpretability, offering new tools for researchers, curators, and educators while promoting open data reuse and interoperability across art historical databases.

title: Drumming for Love
description: Drumming for Love is an award-winning installation and research project by Erze Dinarama in collaboration with Iacopo Neri that investigates the political economy of drought governance and water scarcity along Italy's Po River. Through a multi-layered combination of spatial mapping and digital fabrication, the project translates ecological data and the vibrational communications of riverbed aquatic insects into five custom-built interactive devices. By juxtaposing administrative thresholds with more-than-human communication systems, the work challenges top-down environmental policy, turning scientific measurements and fieldwork into a tactile, sensory counter-device that invites the public to renegotiate shared hydrological futures.

title: Artifacts of the Future - Face Scanner
description: Face Scanner, 2075 is a speculative artwork by Erzë Dinarama, in collaboration with Iacopo Neri for the ETH Zürich exhibition 'Artefacts of the Future,' that critically examines the ambient rise of biometric surveillance and automated facial interpretation. Beyond its narrative framing on visual ethics, the project centers on a custom computational design pipeline developed for Rhinoceros 3D to bridge real-time computer vision and 3D modeling. By capturing live gaze patterns via Google MediaPipe and streaming this spatial data directly into Grasshopper/Rhino, the workflow allows designer to deforms and manipulates 3D geometry with their eyes, and the 3D printed sculpture is one example.

title: Funding of Sight
description: The Funding of Sight is an interactive web artwork, presented at the ECCV Art Gallery, that exposes the political economy of computer vision research by tracing how conference sponsorship ties academic innovation to surveillance and warfare. By combining data visualization, investigative research, and semantic media analysis of a sponsor dataset, the piece shifts from the sanitized public rhetoric of AI hype to the stark, infrastructural realities of military deployment and privacy intrusion. This critical methodology transforms the visualization into a site of institutional reflection, inviting researchers and the public to confront the ethical consequences of academic funding while questioning what forms of sight are being optimized and for whom.

title: Tracce
description: Tracce is a web application developed to enhance the autonomy of people with reduced mobility in the city of Monza by transforming everyday experiences into actionable urban planning data. Centered on a user-experience (UX) and participatory design methodology, the app provides personalized, accessible route planning that factors in sidewalk widths, ramps, and pedestrian lighting, while offering a second path alternative to the standard fastest route. Through a georeferenced crowdsourced reporting system, Tracce empowers citizens to flag physical barriers directly on the map, creating a dynamic data layer that actively assists local authorities in updating and implementing the city's Plan for the Elimination of Architectural Barriers (PEBA).
